**Working entry:** MountedData buffered render — a task polled during render reaches the document: upstream
`286874cc1`'s buffered render on the Dioxus 0.7 bridge, its test the witness, the hazard pin inverted; every Dioxus
document

**Version:** escher-0.3.0 · Epoch 3 — The UI graph · the chunk after `2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe`, before «The UI
graph».

**Why now:** the probe measured the MountedData hazard at HEAD and the founder chose its fix: «Порт, отдельный чанк
(Рекомендую)» — port upstream's buffered render onto the 0.7 bridge in a chunk of its own, after the probe and before
«The UI graph» (`chunks/2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`); the entry is the operator's own
word on the probe's P5 card, row 1 (`chunks/2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/inputs/I3-relay-3.md.txt`). The UI graph
reads the vdom while it renders, so the render must not hold the document.

- **The buffered render on the Dioxus 0.7 bridge** (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/`): `DioxusDocument`'s two render
  sites — `initial_build` (`vdom.rebuild`) and `poll` (`vdom.render_immediate`) — run the vdom into a buffer of
  mutations with the document unborrowed, then take the document's borrow once and apply the buffer through the
  existing `MutationWriter`, then flush the queued mounted events as before. So user code the vdom runs during render —
  a component body, a task it polls — can reach the document (a `MountedData` call: `set_focus`, `get_client_rect`,
  `scroll_to`, `scroll`, `get_scroll_offset`, `get_scroll_size`) with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic.

- **Upstream's regression test as the witness:** `task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` (upstream
  `286874cc1`, `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs`, its `mod tests`) — a task spawned in a component
  body during a re-render calls `set_focus(true)` and `get_client_rect()` on a held `MountedData`, and the focused node
  is the input it named — ported to the 0.7 bridge and passing.

- **The hazard pin inverted:** `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s two `should_panic(expected = "RefCell already borrowed")`
  tests (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_runtime_probe.rs:581`, `:587`, one per layout mode) become tests that the same
  key-handler-spawned task's `set_focus` moves focus and does not panic, in both layout modes, their precondition
  (the handle held; the key target focused by Tab) still asserted first.

- **An engine change for every Dioxus document:** every `DioxusDocument` — the stand, the windowed `dioxus-native`
  launch and any app on the bridge — renders through the buffer. Ratified as the founder's choice of fix
  (`chunks/2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`), no new boundary crossing.

- **CARRY (cry-r2f73kru), folded — the port's shape as read, not run, at the probe** [inferred]: «upstream's
  `mutation_buffer.rs` records Dioxus 0.8's stack-machine mutations, so a 0.7 port records 0.7's `WriteMutations`
  calls in a buffer of its own and replays them into the existing `MutationWriter`, `mutation_writer.rs` kept
  byte-identical to upstream at `434e0661`, `flush_queued_mounted_events` unchanged and its two callers in
  `dioxus_document.rs` changing shape» (read at `doc:2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/report`, Counts / qualifiers
  moved, pattern `buffered`). Re-verified at the take-up, coordinates only: `git diff 434e0661 HEAD --
  packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs` is empty (byte-identical today); the two callers stand at
  `dioxus_document.rs:161–167` (`initial_build`) and `:295–300` (`poll`), `flush_queued_mounted_events` at `:232`;
  upstream `286874cc1` adds `mutation_buffer.rs` (209 lines) and changes those two hunks to
  `vdom.rebuild/render_immediate(&mut self.vdom_state.buffered_mutations)` then
  `self.vdom_state.apply_buffered_mutations(&mut self.inner.borrow_mut())`. The mechanism — that a recorder of 0.7's
  `WriteMutations` calls replayed in order into `MutationWriter` builds the same document as the direct write, and
  that nothing in the render reads the document's state mid-render — is P3's to close.

- **The hazard's mechanism, as the probe measured it** [inferred]: `DioxusDocument::poll` holds `inner.borrow_mut()`
  at `dioxus_document.rs:295` across `vdom.render_immediate` at `:297`; dioxus-core 0.7.10 polls a queued task there
  (`virtual_dom.rs:611`); its `set_focus` (`events.rs:295`) borrows through `doc_mut` (`events.rs:162`) and panics —
  measured in both layout modes by the two pins (`doc:2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/report`, Counts / qualifiers
  moved, the MountedData record). The windowed path read, not run.

- The ruling it stands on: the founder's «Порт, отдельный чанк (Рекомендую)», the fork's text stating «Every fix is an
  engine change for every Dioxus document» (`chunks/2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe/inputs/I2-relay-2.md.txt`).

- **Dioxus stays at 0.7** — the `"0.7.3"` requirement, dioxus-core 0.7.10 in the lock; no 0.8 move, no patch or
  vendored Dioxus crate, no pin bumped. Upstream's 0.8-only parts of `286874cc1` (the stack-machine `WriteMutations`,
  `StackWriter` + `BlitzBackend`, the keyboard-types 0.8 move, `keyboard_compat.rs`'s removal, the `ElementId::from_raw`
  change, the `stale_node_mapping` rewrite, the browser and example adaptations) are not ported.

- **`mutation_writer.rs` kept byte-identical to upstream at `434e0661`** where the port allows [inferred]; a change
  there is named with its reason.

- **Nothing crosses:** no verb, argument, node key, result field, cause, session error, exit, carrier, listener, port,
  env var, workspace crate, log field or span; the buffer holds mutations (ids, tag and attribute names, text) in
  process only, never printed or logged.

- **Behaviour otherwise unchanged:** the document every render builds, the element ids, the snapshot and its diff,
  the mounted events' order and the incremental/non-incremental layout identity stay as they are — the existing

  witness.
- **The UI graph is not built here**; no capability of 0.3.0 is advanced unless P4 finds one this chunk proves.

- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/` — `dioxus_document.rs` (the two render sites, the ported test), a new buffer

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/dioxus_runtime_probe.rs` — the two pins inverted, its module text re-said.

events as now. So a task the vdom polls during render — or any user code it runs there — can reach the document through
`MountedData` (`set_focus`, `get_client_rect`, `scroll_to`, …) with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic. This closes the
measured hazard (architecture/established-decisions fct-apdputpm; security-plan/error-handling fct-7ni72vcj;

   the trait listed method by method) as one entry of an in-order `Vec`, with owned arguments: `ElementId`, the counts
   and `Template` (`Copy`) as they come, the `&'static` names, namespaces and paths as they come, `&AttributeValue`
   cloned, and the two `&str` texts (`create_text_node`, `set_node_text`) copied (upstream's single concatenated string
   arena, `StrSpan`, is the form to follow; a `String` per entry is acceptable). One method,
   `replay(&mut self, to: &mut impl WriteMutations)`, drains the entries in recorded order into `to`, calling the same
   trait method with the same arguments (a recorded `&AttributeValue` passed by reference), and leaves the buffer empty
   with its allocations kept for the next render. The module opens with a `//!` doc saying what it records and why (the
   render runs with the document unborrowed, upstream `286874cc1`, https://github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz/pull/1260); its

   borrow of `self.inner` held; then take `self.inner.borrow_mut()` once, build `MutationWriter::new(&mut inner, &mut
   self.vdom_state)`, call the buffer's `replay` into it, drop the writer and the borrow (the mutator flushes on drop, as

1. **Write `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_buffer.rs`** — a crate-private (`pub(crate)`) `MutationBuffer` that
   implements dioxus-core 0.7.10's `WriteMutations` by recording each of the trait's 15 calls (research, Files inspected:
   the trait listed method by method) as one entry of an in-order `Vec`, with owned arguments: `ElementId`, the counts
   and `Template` (`Copy`) as they come, the `&'static` names, namespaces and paths as they come, `&AttributeValue`
   cloned, and the two `&str` texts (`create_text_node`, `set_node_text`) copied (upstream's single concatenated string
   arena, `StrSpan`, is the form to follow; a `String` per entry is acceptable). One method,
   `replay(&mut self, to: &mut impl WriteMutations)`, drains the entries in recorded order into `to`, calling the same
   trait method with the same arguments (a recorded `&AttributeValue` passed by reference), and leaves the buffer empty
   with its allocations kept for the next render. The module opens with a `//!` doc saying what it records and why (the
   render runs with the document unborrowed, upstream `286874cc1`, https://github.com/DioxusLabs/blitz/pull/1260); its
   type implements `Debug` printing the entry count alone, or none at all; it holds no `trace!`/`tracing` site, print,
   env read, `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` (keeps arch S3 · S4 · S5, obs S2 · S3, security S1 · S4). Gate 8 greps the
   whole file, comments and docs included, so none of its tokens (`print!`, `dbg!`, `std::env`, `env::var`, `trace!`,
   `tracing`, `log::`, `escher_telemetry`, `unwrap(`, `expect(`, `panic!`, `bind(`, the two listener names) is written
   there even in prose.

# Mutation control — the borrowed render restored in `poll` (implement P2, 2026-11-07)

Mutation: `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs`, `poll`'s render site put back to the pre-chunk
shape (`inner.borrow_mut()` → `MutationWriter::new` → `self.vdom.render_immediate(&mut writer)`), `initial_build`
left buffered. Bytes saved before, restored after: sha256
`b4308a9e6e4658d3941de93483afb536cf51d0e8b46979c959f06b25fb4a0f42` before and after (restored True), the restore
read before the green readings were taken as final (the gate block ran green before the mutation, on the same sha).

Readings under the mutation:
- `cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom --locked task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` — exit 0:
  `test dioxus_document::tests::task_polled_during_render_can_access_document ... ok`,
  `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 82 filtered out`.
- `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast --test dioxus_runtime_probe` — exit 101:
  `test mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_incremental ... FAILED`,
  `test mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental ... FAILED` (each `RefCell already
  borrowed`), `test result: FAILED. 8 passed; 2 failed`.

So the inverted probe pins read red without the fix and green with it. Upstream's witness reads green either way on
Dioxus 0.7.

Mechanism (dioxus-core 0.7.10 `src/virtual_dom.rs`, read): the witness's task is spawned from the app's component
body during `render_immediate`'s `Work::RerunScope` arm (`:615–620`). No `queue_events` follows a `RerunScope`, so
the task's `TaskNotified` message stays in the channel, and the next `poll`'s `wait_for_work` → `process_events` →
`poll_tasks` (`:445–519`) polls it with no scope dirty, before the bridge takes any borrow. The probe's key handler
spawns its task and also writes a signal, which dirties a scope. `process_events` then returns before `poll_tasks`,
and the task is first polled inside `render_immediate`'s `Work::PollTask` arm (`:610–613`), where the borrow was held.

## 2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render — the spawned-task MountedData hazard record, closed by the buffered render
**Section:** §5 Keyboard Navigation (keyboard-navigation.md: the MountedData hazard record)
**Change:**
- Was: a `MountedData` call in a task spawned from a key handler that writes a signal panics with `RefCell already borrowed` — `DioxusDocument::poll` holds `inner.borrow_mut()` across `vdom.render_immediate`, where dioxus-core 0.7.10 first polls the task — pinned by `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s two `should_panic` pins, so Cells calls its handles synchronously, the fix routed to the route entry «MountedData buffered render».
- Now: the call acts and does not panic, on every Dioxus document: `DioxusDocument::initial_build` and `Document::poll` render into a mutation buffer (`buffered_mutations`, a `MutationBuffer`) with the document unborrowed, then take `inner.borrow_mut()` once and replay it through one `MutationWriter`, so the task reaches the document through `doc_mut`.
- Its measure: the two pins `mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_{non_incremental,incremental}`, in both layout modes, precondition first, each asserting after the task's `set_focus` that the engine's focus, the snapshot's one `focused` node and the tree's focus name `focus-target`; both read FAILED with the borrowed render restored; the windowed path read and not run.
- Its basis moved from 2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe's report to this chunk's.
**Why:** the chunk ported the founder's chosen fix (his option, relayed at the probe chunk) onto Dioxus 0.7, retiring the panic and the two `should_panic` pins; on the operator's ruling (directly in the implement session, 2026-11-07) that the witness question goes to the wrap to amend the specs, the probe's two pins, discriminating under the mutation control, are the fix's witness on 0.7.
**Kept:** Cells' synchronous handle calls, each acting at the call — no longer needed for the hazard, and kept.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-07T12-33-28-wrap/

## 2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render — the buffered render's same-render limit
**Section:** §5 Keyboard Navigation (keyboard-navigation.md: a new bullet after the MountedData hazard record)
**Change:**
- Added: a task polled during a Dioxus render acts on the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in the same render is not yet in it and `set_focus_to` returns `false` for it; the probe's pins act on nodes mounted by an earlier render; the limit is owned by an open `residual` row (target: next), the body naming no id.
**Why:** the limit holds by construction of the buffered render, as the report states it; the operator's directive at this wrap's resume (the operator, by message, 2026-11-07) records it as an open residual row, target next, P5's append.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-07T12-33-28-wrap/

- Borrow conflicts are worked around by taking a child list or layout out and restoring it, and, on the Dioxus bridge, by rendering the vdom into a crate-private `MutationBuffer` with the document's `RefCell` unborrowed, then borrowing the document once and replaying the buffer through one `MutationWriter`; let-chains in `if` conditions are used.

- `element_to_node_id` unwraps; `NodeHandle::node` panics if the node is gone. `DioxusDocument::initial_build` and `Document::poll` render through the crate-private `MutationBuffer` (`buffered_mutations`) with the document unborrowed, then take `inner.borrow_mut()` once, replay through one `MutationWriter` and drop the writer and the borrow before `flush_queued_mounted_events`, so a task dioxus-core 0.7.10 polls inside `render_immediate` that writes a signal and calls `set_focus` reaches the document through `MountedData` and `doc_mut` with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic — a direct engine change for every Dioxus document, a port of upstream `286874cc1`'s buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge, flagged not upstreamable (upstream holds its 0.8 form), witnessed by `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s two `mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_{non_incremental,incremental}` tests; its limit: a task polled during render acts on the document as the previous render left it, so `set_focus_to` returns `false` for a node created in that same render; Cells still calls its handles synchronously, kept, the hazard not needing it.

- `src/{actionable,dioxus_document,element_id,mutation_writer,mutation_buffer,events,snapshot,snapshot_diff,snapshot_text,write_once_attr,keyboard_compat}.rs` (`mutation_buffer`, crate-private, outside every `accessibility` gate, no `pub use`: the `MutationBuffer` the bridge renders into with the document unborrowed, then replays through one `MutationWriter`) (`keyboard_compat`, crate-private and upstream's since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync, converts keyboard-types 0.8 into Dioxus 0.7's types for `events.rs`, excluded from the coverage leg by filename until escher takes upstream's retirement of it)

- `cargo test -p dioxus-native-dom` (67 unit tests in nine files — six of them upstream's, arrived at 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship: four drop tests in `dioxus_document.rs` (beside them upstream's `task_polled_during_render_can_access_document` from `286874cc1`, as upstream wrote it — it passes, but on Dioxus 0.7 also with the borrowed render restored, so the buffered render's discriminating witness is `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s two `…_spawned_acts_*` tests) and two in `mutation_writer::tests` (test-plan §1);
